keys.explanation: Process and people failures (changes, procedures, maintenance) are major drivers of facility downtime.
Colo security is multi-tenant compartmentalization on top of site controls.

The current NFPA 10 catalog identifies the portable-fire-extinguisher standard. The item keeps agent choice tied to hazard, site policy, and trained use, with CO2 personnel-safety caveats; it does not replace building suppression or authorize untrained intervention.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP-4(a)-(c) requires testing the contingency plan at an organization-defined frequency, reviewing test results, and initiating corrective actions when needed. CP-4(1) adds coordination with organizational elements responsible for related plans, including business-continuity and emergency-related plans. The control does not prescribe a numeric cadence here.

The current eCFR hot-work rule requires controlling nearby fire hazards, authorization, suitable extinguishing equipment, and fire-watch conditions. This item stays at that control boundary and does not invent a site-specific permit form or universal stand-off.
The current IEC catalog lists devices operating at power frequencies, including power lines and electric appliances, as field sources; it does not establish a transformer/busbar/UPS ranking.
The current ISO abstract says ISO/IEC 22237-1:2021 specifies a classification system based on availability, security, and energy-efficiency criteria over the planned lifetime of the data centre.

NFPA 70 (2026) §§700.12 and 700.17 tie emergency lighting to an Article 700 source and an emergency-lighting branch-circuit path when normal lighting fails. IT continuity alone does not prove that life-safety path; an UPS belongs in the answer only after the Article 700 design is verified.
Li-ion offers density and lifecycle trade-offs, not magic immunity from engineering.
Exit signs mark the means of egress; they are life-safety devices.

The IEC catalog defines recirculation and bypass flow rates and associated measurement methods for forced-air-cooled indoor cabinets; it does not expose a particular blanking-panel or brush-strip design rule.
Cold plates remove heat at the component rather than only via room air.
Single-mode supports long reach and high capacity backbone roles; multimode is common for shorter structured runs depending on design.
SPOFs are failure points without concurrent path diversity for the protected load.
Factory trunks reduce field termination variability—still require correct design, pathways, and acceptance tests.
Water balance anomalies are early warnings for plant risk—instrumentation supports response.
A zero-U PDU mounts vertically at the rear or side of the cabinet, preserving horizontal rack U for IT equipment.
Heterogeneous telemetry plus alert quality is the hard problem—not sensor scarcity alone.
Recirculation is hot air returning to intakes instead of the cooling return path.
The IEC catalog explicitly excludes conventional AC and DC distribution boards and their associated switches.
Containment integrity matters—open doors, missing panels, and cable gaps re-create recirculation paths.
Concentrated loads are point/small-area forces that can govern panel and pedestal design.
DCIM ties inventory, power capacity, and change workflows to facilities data—not just environment sensing.
Guides recommend practice; binding force comes from adoption into law, contract, or policy.

The EPA case is useful precisely because its closed-loop reuse system still required makeup water and site-specific rights and permits. DOE FEMP and the NREL ESIF report distinguish recirculating liquid paths and dry or evaporative heat rejection, but neither grants a universal siting permission. ISO/IEC 30134-9:2022 supplies the WUE KPI and measurement categories; it does not turn a project example into a benchmark or permit.

TIA-942-B §1.2 defines requirements but does not mandate or provide an assessment program. 'Designed to TIA-942-B Rated-3' is a self-declaration by the designer or owner — it may or may not have been verified by a third party. A due-diligence reviewer should ask whether an independent assessor validated the claim and, if so, request the assessment report. Self-declaration and third-party assessment are distinct; the marketing phrase does not prove either.
Visitors need controlled credentials and escort; shared badges destroy audit.
A site can have carriers and utilities yet fail resilience if deed restrictions, easements, or landlord constraints block fuel or antenna rights; those are site-selection constraints.
Loading categories match different force patterns: area, point, and rolling traffic.
Distance is the strongest cheap tool for power-frequency magnetic fields.

Logos are not laterals. A shared duct bank or manhole collapses both providers to one backhoe cut. That is the building oral. It is not the east-west fabric: a single-path IB/RoCE mesh remains one training job even if the laterals were actually diverse. Do not invent a reach metre.

Physical security runbooks treat piggybacking as a control failure even during emergencies. Challenge and verify; do not trade access control for speed. Cameras help forensics but do not replace the live access decision.

29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(8) requires required safety data sheets to be readily accessible during each work shift. Paragraph (h)(2)(iii) requires employees to be informed of the location and availability of the written hazard-communication program, hazardous-chemical lists, and safety data sheets; (h)(1) and (h)(3) cover initial/new-hazard information and training content. This is a bounded documentation claim, not a claim that the regulation requires a document titled an OH&S manual.
Correlate related telemetry into incidents to protect on-call attention.

OSHA 1910.147 excludes electrical-hazard exposure in electric-utilization installations, while 1910.333 requires electrical work practices including physical disconnection, stored-energy control, lockout/tagging, verification, and safe re-energization.
Cooling failure can cascade into thermal IT failure even when power is still present.

The current NFPA 1 preview supports treating fire protection and compartmentation as code-governed concerns. An unsealed penetration can compromise a rated barrier and permit smoke or fire spread; the item does not prescribe a project-specific firestop detail or AHJ ruling.
Unverified emergency lighting is a latent life-safety failure.

The ISO preview defines ERF as a KPI to quantify reused energy and gives the ratio of energy being reused divided by the sum of all energy consumed in a data centre. It does not establish a separate ERE taxonomy or a universal target.
The IEC catalog identifies ensuring continuity of load power as the primary function of covered UPS systems.

policy: e2e/harness and post-grade explanations only; not the learner exam payload
